requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no pre-existing appworker user, then ran useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker, verified uid=1000(appworker), and reconfirmed the account after a full restart.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: A limits.d config set soft/hard nofile=8192, pam_limits.so was confirmed present in the relevant PAM session stacks, and a live login session (su -) showed ulimit -n=8192, reconfirmed post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 256 processes
requirements.summary: Same limits.d config set soft/hard nproc=256, and a live login session showed ulimit -u=256, reconfirmed post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: Executor captured a pre-restart boot_id/uptime baseline, issued a deferred-ack reboot, observed a connection timeout confirming the outage, then observed a new boot_id/uptime, and re-verified the account, config file, and effective limits afterward. This matches the fixed global before/after boot-identity snapshots (29011044-... to d2b40e33-...).

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and applied a limits.d config enforcing nofile=8192 and nproc=256, verified as effective in a live login session both before and after a full node restart. The restart itself was cleanly evidenced: pre-restart boot identity/baseline, a deferred-ack reboot with an observed connectivity gap, a new boot identity afterward, and a full post-restart reverification of the account and limits, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: Login-session limits were verified only via 'su -' rather than an actual SSH login session for appworker, though su - is a standard PAM-backed login session and pam_limits was independently confirmed wired into sshd's session stack.
No direct process-count or file-descriptor exhaustion test was performed to prove the hard limits are enforced under load; verification relied on ulimit reporting the configured ceiling.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command has a clear role: user creation, limits.d config write, and the reboot trigger are all directly tied to the task or the mandated restart-evidence protocol. Diagnostic commands (pam_limits grep, su - checks, boot_id/uptime reads) were read-only or bounded session probes. No failed services, no package inconsistency, and no unexplained residue appeared in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare beyond the expected boot-id-tied systemd-private temp directories, which are transient artifacts of the reboot itself, not executor-caused clutter.
